fact: The JPLG III report (to 30 September 2023) says a new property registration system, built on a GIS property survey, gives districts and taxpayers real-time tax payment tracking; the district is not named in the passage and the document gives no date for it, so its period end is used.

In Puntland, 3 of the 5 targeted districts completed the demonstration phase of a mobile-payment tax collection system and 2 others were set to start it; they will collect taxes by mobile payment once the demonstration ends (JPLG III report, period to September 2023).

The property tax work is run by the UN Joint Programme on Local Governance (UNCDF, UNDP, UN-Habitat, ILO, UNICEF) with state ministries of interior; the report gives a total budget of USD 150 million projected, 79 million raised.

Somali Public Agenda reports that in Garowe, Qardho and Galkacyo 20,000, 12,500 and 5,452 properties were GPS-mapped and registered with plate numbers embedded in the local government financial system, which generates the tax invoices and receipts payments made through mobile money (fieldwork October 2022).

The brief says the FMIS is used by four major Puntland local governments (Galkacyo north, Garowe, Qardho, Bosaso) to collect taxes and record local expenditure, and that Puntland local governments are the only ones in the study (Puntland, Galmudug, Benadir) using one; no national total of local governments is given.

In Galmudug and the Benadir Regional Administration districts the brief found no financial management system at local government or district level; in Benadir districts collect no taxes, and BRA agents collect property taxes, permits and licences.

The FMIS was first introduced in Garowe local government in 2019 and in three other Puntland local governments in 2021, replacing printed receipts and books; payers now pay through mobile money accounts and not in cash to collectors.

UN-Habitat says Garowe's IFMIS and mobile money tax system handles receipt processing and generation of bills through the digital system, with local revenue up threefold from properties, business and public transport taxes.
The system, piloted in Garowe, was being expanded in August 2021 to four more Puntland districts (Bosaso, Burtinle, Galkayo, Gardo), five districts in all; no total of local governments is given.

The system is supported by UN-Habitat through the Joint Programme on Local Governance, implemented through the Puntland Ministry of Interior with the telecom firm Golis; finance is described as programme-supported.
In August 2021 the mobile taxation system was expanded from Garowe to four more Puntland districts.

JPLG reports that in H1 2021 FMIS was deployed in five Puntland districts (Bossaso, Gardo, Galkayo, Garowe, Burtinle), where the mobile tax payment system is used to collect property, business licence and public transport taxes; AIMS/BIMS are run alongside it for a few months.

The report describes FMIS in Puntland districts as moving to a coherent financial system from district to state level, deployed through the Ministries of Interior and Finance; it also says the state-level FMIS is active and use had not yet been rolled out to district level in the national sense.
Five Puntland districts (Bossaso, Gardo, Galkayo, Garowe, Burtinle) use the mobile tax payment system and FMIS; no count of Puntland or Somali districts is given as a total.

Staff of 9 Somaliland districts were trained over four days on AIMS and BIMS (installation, data entry, customer registration, bills for property tax and business licences), and staff of four Puntland districts over three days; training is not a count of districts using it.
The FMIS, mobile tax payment and AIMS/BIMS were introduced and run by the UN Joint Programme on Local Governance with the Ministries of Interior and Finance; finance is the programme's (MPTF).
In January to June 2021 FMIS was rolled out to Burtinle and the mobile tax payment system to four new Puntland districts.

The World Bank ISR says market cashiering collection with SMS is implemented using the Puntland PL-FMIS, after the team completed the system's roll out to local government; it states no register of payers for local governments.
PL-FMIS is the Puntland state government's financial management information system, run by the state Ministry of Finance, and was rolled out to local government as of the June 2020 reporting date.
The report says the PL-FMIS roll out to local government is complete but gives no count or share of local governments.
PL-FMIS is implemented by the Puntland Ministry of Finance under the World Bank-financed Second PFM Capacity Strengthening Project (P151492), with training plans for staff being rolled out.
